BROKER HEALTH REQUIREMENT TESTED: checkHealth freshly authenticates and validates every granted named operation, not only previously used resource IDs, in BEGIN READ ONLY. It checks schema USAGE, SELECT-only table/column access, relation/type safety and referenced-column existence, then PREPARE/DEALLOCATE checks SQL operators without executing application queries or accepting buyer inputs. Real tests pass initial health then revoke SELECT on the second operation, rotate the password, add UPDATE, revoke schema USAGE and rename a column; each subsequent probe fails. An RLS function that raises on row access permits health but fails real execution, proving health does not read application rows. Fixed deadline/concurrency and lock/cancellation tests passed. This establishes the package health API; host READY publication, representative output validation and paid-job end-to-end behavior remain separate evidence.

FULL NARROW READ-ONLY PROOF: real PostgreSQL rejects reader INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/DDL/COPY and server-file access with SQLSTATE 42501 even after default_transaction_read_only is disabled. A separate administrator BEGIN READ ONLY transaction rejects UPDATE with SQLSTATE 25006. Both execution and checkHealth verify transaction_read_only and role/table/column privilege safety; a new health regression grants UPDATE after initial successful approval/probe and verifies the next probe refuses readiness. These are executed database safety proofs, not mocks or a claim that worker readiness consumes the API automatically.
